svg.title: Four Checks Before Valuing a Claim
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-lane-specific-preflight-decision-tree; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Checks Before Valuing a Claim; subtitle: Test the selected lane, then apply the shared authority and cash check.; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: The first three nodes are alternative lane branches; an eligible branch proceeds to the fourth shared check. A failed eligibility test stops that lane unless a documented correction remains possible. Documentation budgets are incremental purchased-evidence costs per paid account and exclude contractor labor. Cash windows are illustrative planning intervals from a complete filing to receipt, not agency or administrator service commitments.; caption: Separate eligibility, collectible base, evidence expense, surety exposure, and payment timing before assigning expected fee value.; stages: label: Drawback eligibility; value: If eligible, continue to shared check; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Apply 19 U.S.C. § 1313 and 19 CFR Part 190, including the applicable export or destruction requirements and generally the five-year claim-completion limit measured from importation. Exclude duties barred from drawback, including antidumping and countervailing duties. Base value on qualifying refundable duty components after statutory limits. Budget $1,500 in evidence cost per paid account. Accelerated payment requires applicable CBP authorization and bond coverage; without it, plan standard payment. Model 6–18 months for standard recovery, potentially longer.; label: Tariff-refund route; value: Choose correction or timely protest; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Use PSC only for eligible unliquidated entries, ordinarily within 300 days of entry and at least 15 days before scheduled liquidation, whichever deadline arrives first. Use 19 U.S.C. § 1514 protests generally within 180 days of liquidation or the applicable protestable decision. Base value on substantiated overpaid duties. Budget $1,200 per paid account. An ordinary refund request has no drawback accelerated-payment bond, although existing entry bonds remain separate. Model 3–12 months after a complete filing, potentially longer.; label: Settlement class eligibility; value: Validate the actual court-defined class; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Use the settlement order, claim deadline, class period, allocation plan, and Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23. Check claimant identity, exclusions, releases, assignments, and duplicate submissions. The collectible base is the eventual allocated distribution, not purchase volume or the settlement fund. Budget $600 per paid account. Ordinary administrative claim filing generally requires no customs surety bond; inspect the actual order for separate security terms. Model 6–24 months or longer, especially when appeals delay distribution.; label: Authority and cash capacity; value: Proceed only with supported execution; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Verify broker or trade-counsel authority and valid Customs Powers of Attorney for formal CBP filings, Part 190 records for drawback, and court-required third-party filer disclosures for settlements explaining direct filing at zero cost. Confirm surety capacity before requesting accelerated payment. If collateral exceeds available capital, use the standard-payment route or defer the account; never fund operations from client principal.

text.title: Four Checks Before Valuing a Claim
text.tspan: Four Checks Before Valuing a Claim

rect.title: label: Drawback eligibility; value: If eligible, continue to shared check; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Apply 19 U.S.C. § 1313 and 19 CFR Part 190, including the applicable export or destruction requirements and generally the five-year claim-completion limit measured from importation. Exclude duties barred from drawback, including antidumping and countervailing duties. Base value on qualifying refundable duty components after statutory limits. Budget $1,500 in evidence cost per paid account. Accelerated payment requires applicable CBP authorization and bond coverage; without it, plan standard payment. Model 6–18 months for standard recovery, potentially longer.

text.title: Apply 19 U.S.C. § 1313 and 19 CFR Part 190, including the applicable export or destruction requirements and generally the five-year claim-completion limit measured from importation. Exclude duties barred from drawback, including antidumping and countervailing duties. Base value on qualifying refundable duty components after statutory limits. Budget $1,500 in evidence cost per paid account. Accelerated payment requires applicable CBP authorization and bond coverage; without it, plan standard payment. Model 6–18 months for standard recovery, potentially longer.

rect.title: label: Tariff-refund route; value: Choose correction or timely protest; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Use PSC only for eligible unliquidated entries, ordinarily within 300 days of entry and at least 15 days before scheduled liquidation, whichever deadline arrives first. Use 19 U.S.C. § 1514 protests generally within 180 days of liquidation or the applicable protestable decision. Base value on substantiated overpaid duties. Budget $1,200 per paid account. An ordinary refund request has no drawback accelerated-payment bond, although existing entry bonds remain separate. Model 3–12 months after a complete filing, potentially longer.

text.title: Use PSC only for eligible unliquidated entries, ordinarily within 300 days of entry and at least 15 days before scheduled liquidation, whichever deadline arrives first. Use 19 U.S.C. § 1514 protests generally within 180 days of liquidation or the applicable protestable decision. Base value on substantiated overpaid duties. Budget $1,200 per paid account. An ordinary refund request has no drawback accelerated-payment bond, although existing entry bonds remain separate. Model 3–12 months after a complete filing, potentially longer.

rect.title: label: Settlement class eligibility; value: Validate the actual court-defined class; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Use the settlement order, claim deadline, class period, allocation plan, and Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23. Check claimant identity, exclusions, releases, assignments, and duplicate submissions. The collectible base is the eventual allocated distribution, not purchase volume or the settlement fund. Budget $600 per paid account. Ordinary administrative claim filing generally requires no customs surety bond; inspect the actual order for separate security terms. Model 6–24 months or longer, especially when appeals delay distribution.

text.title: Use the settlement order, claim deadline, class period, allocation plan, and Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23. Confirm surety capacity before requesting accelerated payment. If collateral exceeds available capital, use the standard-payment route or defer the account; never fund operations from client principal.

Assumptions: The first three nodes are alternative lane branches; an eligible branch proceeds to the fourth shared check. A failed eligibility test stops that lane unless a documented correction remains possible. Documentation budgets are incremental purchased-evidence costs per paid account and exclude contractor labor. Cash windows are illustrative planning intervals from a complete filing to receipt, not agency or administrator service commitments.
